newsitem.title: USA: SEC drops insider trading case against London man.
newsitem.headline: SEC drops insider trading case against London man.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday it has dropped insider trading charges against a London businessman involving trades in APL Ltd because of lack of evidence.
The SEC said it "voluntarily dismissed" its civil insider trading claim against Abdul Ismail, one of three defendents named in its April civil case filed in U.S. District Court in Manhattan.

"Based on all the evidence gathered since the case was filed, the Commission has determined that it lacks sufficient evidence to continue prosecuting its claims against Ismail at this time," the agency said.
The case continues against two Singapore men named in the April suit, the SEC said.
The agency had alleged that the three men purchased APL shares in advance of a public announcement that the company would be acquired in a merger with Neptune Orient Lines Ltd.

Charges were filed by the SEC based on the timing and volume of the purchases, officials said. The agency accused Ismail of insider trading because he bought about $228,000 in APL stock options on April 11, 1997, which nearly doubled in value after the merger was announced two days later.
An attorney representing the London businessman said his client was happy with the SEC's latest decision.

"Mr. Ismail informed us from the first that he had purchased the securities soley on his own study of the company and that he had absolutely no insider information. All the evidence sustained that," said Mortin Gold, an attorney with the New York firm, Gold Farrell and Marks.

Gold noted that Ismail cooperated fully with the SEC's inquiries. "We were confident that the case would go the way it did," he said, adding that Ismail reserves the right to recover from the SEC the costs and damages associated with the case.
